brief.attributes: Navigation as accumulated inference: each revealed or exiled possibility narrows the course.

candidate.text: Freedom began as timber, measured and cut by hand.
candidate.basis: Odysseus personally selects, cuts, smooths and joins the timber for his raft.
candidate.fit: Keeps the emphasis on earned agency rather than miraculous rescue.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked: Odysseus personally selects trees, cuts them, adzes them smooth, joins the timbers and launches the raft.
brief.attributes: Self-rescue through competent labour; no god carries him away for free.

candidate.text: Each crossing taught the crew what the next storm would demand.
candidate.basis: Book V treats sea travel as repeated endurance and adaptation; this card generalises that voyage pattern.
candidate.fit: Composite voyage flavour rather than a claim of one specific gale-rowing scene.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked as voyage composite: repeated endurance at sea is explicit, but quest counters, Treasure and card access are gameplay abstractions.
brief.attributes: Persistence converts repeated dangerous passage into preparedness and options.

candidate.text: Before a ship can brave the sea, someone must master fire beside it.
candidate.basis: Book V directly supplies shipbuilding craft but not a shipyard spark incident.
candidate.fit: Explicit material-world extension.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for shipbuilding craft; the spark incident and dedicated shipyard setting are explicit material-world extensions.

candidate.text: The tool that shaped the raft made every later mile possible.
candidate.basis: Calypso gives Odysseus an adze, which he uses in the raft construction.
candidate.fit: Source-led object flavour without quoting another Book V line.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked: Calypso gives Odysseus a sharp adze and he uses it to shape the raft.
brief.attributes: A practical tool whose value comes from the worker and the vessel it helps create.

candidate.text: Songs survive because memory changes them just enough to sing again.
candidate.basis: Demodocus performs multiple stories and listeners repeatedly ask for more.
candidate.fit: Original oral-performance interpretation for the refrain/enchantment engine.

brief.sourceReview: Book VIII checked: songs are repeated, requested and heard differently by listeners. 'Refrain' plus Constellation is an oral-performance interpretation.
brief.attributes: Memory becomes usable when a familiar story returns in a new context.

candidate.text: The horizon vanished before the sailor had time to name the weather.
candidate.basis: Poseidon's storm rapidly covers earth, sea and sky with cloud.
candidate.fit: Keeps this common squall below the named divine-storm card.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked: Poseidon's storm violently stops progress. This common is intentionally a smaller generic squall rather than another divine named event.

candidate.text: A house stands because something bears its weight.
candidate.basis: The Phaeacian palace is described through elaborate architecture and crafted supports; a living Caryatid remains a Theros visual borrowing.
candidate.fit: Original visual-world flavour, not a claim of a Homeric plant-person.

brief.sourceReview: Book VII checked for lavish Phaeacian architecture and crafted supports. A living Caryatid is a Theros/reprint visual borrowing, not a Homeric creature.

candidate.text: Every stronger hull remembers the hands that worked it.
candidate.basis: Odysseus's raft construction supplies the craft vocabulary; the dedicated shipboard carpenter is invented.
candidate.fit: Makes the extension feel ordinary rather than legendary.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for hands-on raft construction. A dedicated shipboard carpenter is an ordinary craft composite, not a named companion.
brief.attributes: The unnoticed specialist whose work becomes visible only when the vessel performs better.

candidate.text: A flawed vessel is not wasted if the next one is better.
candidate.basis: Scheria is rich in household craft, but no specific potter is narrated.
candidate.fit: Original craft flavour for the discard-and-replace mechanic.

brief.sourceReview: Book VII checked for a craft-rich household; no specific potter or kiln scene is narrated. Keep this as material-world extension.

candidate.text: Craft begins with what the household already has.
candidate.basis: Book VII emphasises bronze, gold, silver and skilled household manufacture but names no bowl-smith.
candidate.fit: Original extension tied to the artifact condition.

brief.sourceReview: Book VII checked for bronze, gold, silver and exceptional household craft; the specialist bowl-smith is an invented material-world worker.

candidate.text: Four days of careful work met one angry sea.
candidate.basis: Odysseus completes the raft in four days before Poseidon later destroys it.
candidate.fit: Captures the raft's vulnerability without another direct quotation.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked: the raft is carefully constructed over four days, then battered and finally broken by Poseidon's storm.
brief.attributes: Improvised mobility: enough craft to leave captivity, never enough durability to feel safe.

candidate.text: Hospitality does not end when the feast does.
candidate.basis: Arete orders a proper bed prepared for Odysseus after the meal.
candidate.fit: Turns bedding into continuation of guest-right.

brief.sourceReview: Book VII checked: after supper Arete has a proper bed made for the stranger in the gatehouse.

candidate.text: The sea returned him alive, but not untouched.
candidate.basis: Odysseus reaches shore exhausted, swollen and full of seawater.
candidate.fit: A general mariner line grounded in the storm aftermath.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked as composite: Odysseus reaches shore physically ruined by sea travel. This anonymous mariner generalises that survivor image.

candidate.text: A sailor who reads the water acts before the wave decides for him.
candidate.basis: Odysseus studies surf, rocks, current and shelter while trying to land.
candidate.fit: Explicit seamanship interpretation rather than a named Homeric technique.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked with seamanship extension: Odysseus reads surf, rocks, current and shelter while seeking a landing; 'read the swell' is the card's compressed technique.

candidate.text: The crew trusted the sailor who knew when motion should become patience.
candidate.basis: The voyage repeatedly alternates action with waiting for usable conditions.
candidate.fit: Original weatherwise-sailor composite.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked as seamanship composite: wind, stars, rudder and changing conditions are explicit; the dedicated weatherwise sailor is invented.

candidate.text: Poseidon broke in moments what patience had built in days.
candidate.basis: The storm smashes the raft Odysseus had spent days constructing.
candidate.fit: The Elemental is a game personification of the destructive sea.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked: Poseidon's storm breaks the raft. The Elemental is a game personification of destructive weather, not a creature in Homer.

candidate.text: Hospitality begins by raising the stranger from the ashes.
candidate.basis: Alcinous raises the suppliant from the hearth before seating him.
candidate.fit: Source-led adaptation distinct from the exact quote used on Seat the Guest.

brief.sourceReview: Book VII checked: Alcinous physically raises Odysseus from the hearth and moves him from ash-covered supplication into the household's protected space.

candidate.text: Their ships seemed to know the destination before the sailors spoke it.
candidate.basis: Alcinous says Phaeacian ships understand their passengers' intended destination.
candidate.fit: The shipwright is invented; the impossible craft is directly Homeric.

brief.sourceReview: Book VIII checked: Phaeacian ships are described as knowing destinations and needing no pilots. The individual shipwright is an extension built from that impossible craft culture.
brief.attributes: A maker whose workmanship is so advanced that the finished ship seems to possess intention.

candidate.text: On a bare coast, weather has nowhere to hide its violence.
candidate.basis: Odysseus's landfall is exposed to storm, surf and rock.
candidate.fit: Landscape extension rather than a distinct named storm.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for storm, surf and exposed rock. 'Storm over Limestone' is a landscape extension rather than a separately narrated event.

candidate.text: A useful thing often begins with discarding the failed one.
candidate.basis: Book V supplies intensive practical making; the iterative bench-work engine is an extension.
candidate.fit: Original craft-process flavour.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for practical construction; iterative bench-crafting and artifact filtering are explicit design extensions.
brief.attributes: Craft as revision: useful work comes from recognizing which version to abandon.

candidate.text: No sea was wide enough to delay the messenger of Zeus.
candidate.basis: Hermes crosses land and sea in divine sandals to deliver Zeus's order.
candidate.fit: Specific to Hermes while remaining an adaptation of the narration.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked: Hermes crosses land and sea in golden sandals to deliver Zeus's command. The reprint is a direct visual analogy, not gear Odysseus receives.
brief.attributes: Divine speed made portable: the equipment evokes the messenger, not ownership by the hero.

candidate.text: Speed is another kind of shelter when the sea turns hostile.
candidate.basis: Ordinary fast-galley play is a seamanship extension distinct from supernatural Phaeacian ships.
candidate.fit: Original extension for evasive Vehicle play.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for sea-speed and danger; this ordinary evasive galley is a seamanship extension distinct from the self-knowing Phaeacian ships.
brief.attributes: A fast mortal vessel that survives by staying ahead of small obstacles rather than ignoring the sea.

candidate.text: Immortality was only another name for never leaving.
candidate.basis: Calypso offers immortality if Odysseus remains, while he longs for home.
candidate.fit: Separates the mythic shelter fantasy from a freely chosen happy ending.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked: Calypso's beautiful island and immortality offer make staying genuinely tempting, while Odysseus's homesickness makes the same safety a captivity.
brief.attributes: The mythic version magnifies the seductive stasis: hidden futures grow stronger the longer departure is postponed.

candidate.text: Every thread carried the patience of a household built to last.
candidate.basis: Book VII explicitly praises Phaeacian weaving; dyeing is an invented textile extension.
candidate.fit: Original flavour avoids inventing a named dyer.

brief.sourceReview: Book VII checked: Phaeacian women are explicitly renowned for weaving; dyeing and this specific courtyard worker are textile-world extensions.

candidate.text: A deed ends. The song decides how long it lives.
candidate.basis: Book VIII repeatedly turns heroic action into performed memory and future song.
candidate.fit: Original articulation of kleos through performance.

brief.sourceReview: Book VIII checked for heroic deeds becoming song, reputation and future memory. Kleos is a Greek conceptual frame rather than Butler's English terminology.
brief.attributes: Renown exists after the action: the hero supplies the deed, but other people decide whether it becomes story.

candidate.text: Seven years can feel like one long afternoon when nothing is allowed to change.
candidate.basis: Odysseus recounts seven years on Ogygia; literal time distortion is not in Homer.
candidate.fit: Makes the time metaphor explicit without claiming time travel.

brief.sourceReview: Books V and VII checked: Odysseus stays on Ogygia for seven years amid comfort and tears. Literal altered time is an interpretive metaphor, not a Homeric phenomenon.
brief.attributes: Stasis made seductive: a place can be beautiful enough to hide how much life is being postponed.

candidate.text: Every exposed shore taught the wind a different voice.
candidate.basis: Book V is saturated with shifting wind and exposed sea travel; the named isle is invented.
candidate.fit: Landscape-composite flavour.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for exposed island/sea weather. Windswept Isle is an invented unnamed landscape composite.

candidate.text: Pride entered the games before any athlete did.
candidate.basis: The Phaeacian games turn hospitality into competition, insult and restitution.
candidate.fit: Original line for a later-laurel visual shorthand.

brief.sourceReview: Book VIII checked for the Phaeacian public games. Laurel is later visual shorthand rather than an Odyssey prize detail.

candidate.text: A strange shore can resemble home for exactly as long as the shade lasts.
candidate.basis: The palm imagery comes from Odysseus's speech to Nausicaa; Palmshade Cove itself is invented.
candidate.fit: Source-led landscape interpretation without relocating the Delos palm literally.

brief.sourceReview: Book VI checked: Odysseus compares Nausicaa to a young palm at Delos. Palmshade Cove is an invented landscape treatment, not that literal palm's location.

candidate.text: The best course is the one the sea has already begun to reveal.
candidate.basis: Book V shows navigation through stars, winds, coast and current; the unified system is a composite.
candidate.fit: Original UR navigation flavour.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked as seamanship composite: navigation by stars, wind, coast and current is explicit; the unified exile/Vehicle reading engine is a set-level abstraction.
brief.attributes: Experience turned into prediction: spells and ships are two ways of learning the same dangerous sea.

brief.sourceReview: Books VI–VIII checked for Scheria's harbour and coast. Basic land treatment selected with no flavour text.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for the long open-sea crossing. Basic land treatment selected with no flavour text.

brief.sourceReview: Book V checked for Ogygia's shore and surrounding sea. Basic land treatment selected with no flavour text.
